reference.source: Parsons' Diseases of the Eye 23rd Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
reference.pathophysiology: Alkali hydroxyl ions saponify cell membranes marching into anterior chamber while iron ferrous ions oxidise depositing in epithelia (heterochromia) and retina (degeneration); rebleed clot retraction around day five reopens torn vessels, and siderotic retina fails on ERG before vision subjectively fades.
additionalDifferentials: Alkali versus acid by penetration and irrigation volume
Open versus closed globe by Seidel, chamber depth and pupil shape
Siderosis versus simple cataract by heterochromia and ERG
additionalInvestigations: pH testing after irrigation to neutrality
CT orbit for metallic fragments (no MRI first)
ERG and serial pressure in retained iron
